text:
sanjay.k: Heads up — seeing a bunch of all-reduce stalls on us-west-2 after the overnight infra push. ~6 nodes, training jobs hang in NCCL, not just slow.

maria.sre: Which push? OFED/firmware or kernel?

deploy-bot: deploy #infra/ofed-upgrade to us-west-2 completed @ 2026-03-17T03:12:07Z (image: ofed-5.1.0-rc3, mlx5-fw-46.0).

alex.gpu: Can you paste the NCCL error logs?

sanjay.k: short snippet from worker-az1-005:

```
NCCL WARN Call to cuCommInit returned 11[2026-03-17 04:21:33]
NCCL INFO AllReduce op rank 0 timeout after 120s
[...blocked on ncclRecv/ncclSend...]
```

kevin.net: I ran quick ib_read_bw on one affected node vs a healthy one. Numbers are ~30% of expected for large messages.

sanjay.k: We saw packet retransmits on mlx5 port: ethtool -S shows rx_errors up, and `dmesg` has repeated mlx5_core timeouts.

alex.gpu: Any difference in kernel version between old and new nodes?

sanjay.k: All nodes got kernel 6.4.2-rt, previously 5.15.0 for the stable pool. The ofed/driver package also upgraded mlx5 to 5.1.0-rc3.

maria.sre: Quick mitigation: can we force jobs to TCP fallback to stop hangs? e.g., set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for the job runtime. That will increase latency but keep training alive.

alex.gpu: Confirmed on a repro host: exporting NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 allows all-reduce to finish, but throughput drops heavily (as expected).

kevin.net: Repro steps I ran locally:
```
ssh worker-az1-005
ibv_devinfo -v
# shows active mlx5_0 with GUID changes
ib_read_bw -s 1024 -d mlx5_0
# result: ~6.5GB/s vs expected ~22GB/s
```

sanjay.k: Also noticed MTU mismatch after the OFED package; ibstat shows GID table differences and some ports in PORT_ACTIVE but error counters climbing.

maria.sre: Can we roll the OFED package back on the affected nodes? What's the risk/time?

deploy-bot: rollback plan available: ofed-5.1.0-rc3 -> ofed-5.0.8-stable. Staged script: /opt/rollbacks/ofed-rollback.sh

kevin.net: I can coordinate a targeted rollback for the 6 affected hosts. Will schedule 30m maintenance window for each (drain jobs first).

alex.gpu: Before rollback, let's try a NIC driver rebind (mlx5_core reload) and reflash firmware on one node as a faster test. If that fixes counters, we can pick the minimal path.

sanjay.k: Did a quick rebind on worker-az1-005: `modprobe -r mlx5_core && modprobe mlx5_core` — ports came back but errors resumed after 20m under NCCL load. Firmware reflash is more invasive.

maria.sre: Action items:
- kevin.net -> schedule rollback for affected nodes (start with 2 canaries)
- alex.gpu -> run full `ibv_devinfo`, `ethtool -S`, `dmesg` capture and attach to the ticket
- sanjay.k -> add NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 to job wrapper for current renter pool to prevent further hung runs (short-term)

sanjay.k: Also creating an incident ticket and tagging capacity-impact. This bumped 12 training runs into slower mode -> cost spike (est +25% token-hour for the window).

kevin.net: I'll coordinate with scheduling to avoid triggering autoscaling compensation during rollback.

maria.sre: Long-term: decide whether to pin to older OFED/firmware until mlx5 driver vendors sign off on kernel 6.4. Recommend we block kernel 6.4 in the stable GPU pool until we validate.

alex.gpu: Noted — also adding a perf test that runs ib_read_bw + NCCL microbench on every post-upgrade host before marking ready. That would catch regressions early.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0452 (label: networking, severity: high, owner: kevin.net)

sanjay.k: For the incident notes: repro steps, node list, current mitigations (NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1), and rollback plan attached.

kevin.net: I'll roll back two canaries in the next 15m, report results here.

maria.sre: If canaries look good, we'll schedule remainder in off-peak waves. Keep the workaround env var in place until all nodes are validated.

sanjay.k: Thanks — ping me on pager if anything flips. :eyes:

alex.gpu: FYI for docs: add a post-upgrade smoke that validates NCCL all-reduce at 1x and 10x message sizes (we missed the large message regression).

kevin.net: Canaries done: worker-az1-005 and worker-az2-002 rolled back to ofed-5.0.8; NCCL returns to baseline, ib_read_bw ~22GB/s, no mlx5 timeouts seen after 40m of load.

maria.sre: Good — proceed with remainder, staggered. Also update release notes to recommend keeping kernel 5.15 for gpu-prod until vendor cert.

sanjay.k: I'll update the runbook with the fast mitigation (NCCL_IB_DISABLE) and rollback steps. Closing this thread for now — continuing in INC-2026-0452.

kevin.net: will add a postmortem once rollback wave is done.
